title: Can you lose your salvation?
intro: The Bible contains both strong promises that God keeps his people and serious warnings against falling away. Traditions weigh these differently.

views.label: True believers will persevere
views.summary: Reformed Christians and many Baptists teach that those God has truly saved will be kept by him and persevere to the end (“once saved, always saved” in popular form). Those who fall away completely show they were never truly born again.
views.source: Westminster Confession, Chapter 17; Baptist Faith and Message, Article V

views.label: A believer can fall away
views.summary: Methodists, Pentecostals, Lutherans and many others teach that a real believer can turn away from God and lose salvation, though God’s grace invites them back. The warnings of Hebrews are real.
views.source: Methodist Articles of Religion, Article XII; Augsburg Confession, Article XII

views.label: Grace can be lost by grave sin and restored
views.summary: Catholic teaching holds that mortal sin destroys sanctifying grace, which can be restored through repentance and the sacrament of Reconciliation.

views.label: Salvation is a lifelong journey
views.summary: Orthodox Christians usually avoid speaking of salvation as a finished possession; it is a lifelong process of growing in God by grace, in which people freely cooperate. One may stray and return.
views.source: Fr Thomas Hopko, The Orthodox Faith, vol. 4

common: All agree that salvation depends on God’s grace, that God is faithful, and that Christians are called to keep trusting and following Christ.
